items.author: yehsuf
items.body:
When `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is `"on"`, the agent's working directory is a temporary directory (e.g. `/tmp/...`) rather than the workspace root. This breaks relative paths, `git` commands, build tools, and any tool that expects to run from the project root.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Enable `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled: "on"`
2. Ask the agent to run `pwd` or `git status`

**Expected behavior**

CWD should default to the workspace root.

**Environment**

- VS Code Copilot Chat 0.46.2
- Linux
items.title: Chat agent sandbox sets CWD to temp directory instead of workspace root

items.author: yehsuf
items.body:
When `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is `"on"`, the sandbox configuration (including `allowWrite`, `denyRead` paths) is written to a JSON file inside the same temp directory that is included in `allowWrite`. A sandboxed process can read and overwrite this file before restrictions are enforced, potentially escalating its own permissions.

**Expected behavior**

The settings file should be stored outside the writable temp directory, or be mounted read-only inside the sandbox.

**Environment**

- VS Code Copilot Chat 0.46.2
- Linux
items.title: Sandbox settings file is writable by sandboxed process, allowing self-modification of restrictions

items.author: yehsuf
items.body:
The sandbox defaults to `denyRead: [$HOME]` per the VS Code docs, but there is no documented setting to override this. Users who need the agent to read files in their home directory (dotfiles, config files, etc.) have no supported way to permit it.

**Expected behavior**

There should be a setting (e.g. `chat.agent.sandbox.allowRead`) to override the default deny list.

**Environment**

- VS Code Copilot Chat 0.46.2
- Linux
items.title: No settings-level way to override default denyRead: [$HOME] in chat agent sandbox

## Summary

Allow users to configure the working directory for a chat agent session, defaulting to the workspace root.

## Motivation

Currently the sandbox sets CWD to a temporary directory (see #5097). Even after that bug is fixed, there are legitimate use cases for running an agent session rooted at a specific subdirectory — e.g. a monorepo where only one package is in scope for the session.

- **Default:** CWD is the workspace root (fixing the current bug)
- **Per-session override:** A UI affordance or slash command to set the session root at session start (e.g. `/roo
items.title: Feature request: configurable session root / CWD for chat agent sandbox
